images.alt: How Do Particles Move?. A longitudinal sound wave moves through the medium while particles vibrate about equilibrium.
Compressions and Rarefactions. A longitudinal sound wave moves through the medium while particles vibrate about equilibrium.
Tracking a Particle. A longitudinal sound wave moves through the medium while particles vibrate about equilibrium.
Particles in a solid vibrate along the direction of a travelling compression. Elastic interactions transmit the disturbance; particle spacing alone does not determine sound speed.
Water particles form alternating compressions and rarefactions. The pressure disturbance travels across the liquid. Water’s resistance to compression helps it transmit sound faster than air.
Air particles form alternating high and low density regions. The pressure disturbance carries energy through the gas; the particles do not travel with the wave.
Sound power, the energy transferred each second, passes through a marked area. Intensity equals power divided by area, measured in watts per square metre.

Concentric circles represent spherical wavefronts. Two equal-sized detector areas receive different amounts of power: the farther detector receives less because the sound spreads over a larger sphere.
